newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian farm minister named deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Russian farm minister named deputy PM.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin named Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun a deputy prime minister on Monday, giving Russia's bloated, beleaguered farm lobby a senior voice in the government's reformist cabinet.
"The president signed a decree appointing Khlystun to the new post," a Kremlin spokesman said. "He will also retain his current ministerial post."

Khlystun, who became agriculture minister in March under a dramatic government reshuffle which swept away conservatives, becomes the seventh deputy prime minister in the new-look cabinet. There are also two first deputy prime ministers.

The March shakeup removed Alexander Zaveryukha, a conservative deputy prime minister who presided over Russia's worst harvests in three decades. Zaveryukha was acting agriculture minister before being replaced by Khlystun in May 1996.
The changes had left Russia's giant farm lobby without a cabinet-level voice during the critical spring sowing season.
Khlystun was also farm minister from November 1991 to October 1994, when he resigned that post.
Russia's collective farms have been privatised but are largely unable to cast off the Soviet legacy of inefficiency.
Tight coffers mean there is not enough cash for the sector, but funding levels are still high compared to other countries.
Khlystun has said he is committed to reforming the sector, but he faces a monumental task in helping farms make the transition to a market environment.
He is seeking to raise money for the sector through commercial banks and he wants to rely less on government handouts, subsidies and barter operations.
Imports make up about 40 percent of Russia's food market as food output has plummeted.
The last two grain harvests have been Russia's worst in 30 years but the government does not have the cash to import the vast quantities of wheat and feed grains that it did in the 1970s.
